video_metadata.working_title: WASHINGTON 1986 Cold Case Solved After 32 Years — Justice for Michella Welch
video_metadata.topic_one_sentence: In March 1986, 12-year-old Michella Welch vanished from Puget Park in North Tacoma while looking after her two younger sisters; for 32 years her killing was wrongly assumed to be linked to the murder of 13-year-old Jennifer Bastian, until DNA split the cases and genetic genealogy plus a discarded restaurant napkin led to the June 2018 arrest of nurse Gary Charles Hartman, convicted in March 2022.
video_metadata.primary_emotion_to_evoke: grief turning into dignified, hard-won justice

protagonist._instructions: Main character. For this channel the victim is the heart of the story; the convicted man is described through records only.
protagonist.full_name: Michella Evon Welch (victim, central character). Convicted offender: Gary Charles Hartman.
protagonist.age_at_time_of_events: Michella: 12 (born 1973, sixth grader). Hartman: 66 at arrest in June 2018 and 70 at sentencing in March 2022, so roughly 33-34 in March 1986 (derived).
protagonist.occupation_or_status: Michella: sixth-grade student in Tacoma, oldest of three sisters. Hartman: registered nurse, described as a community nurse specialist at Western State Hospital in Lakewood at the time of his arrest.
protagonist.location: Tacoma (North End / North Tacoma), Pierce County, Washington. Hartman lived in Lakewood in 2018 and, according to records cited by ABC News, less than two miles from Puget Park in 1986.
protagonist.physical_description: Not used. Only real archival photos released by family/police may be shown.
protagonist.background_brief: Michella was the oldest of three girls. On a Wednesday in March 1986 she was in charge of her two younger sisters at Puget Park. Her sister Nicole Eby later described her as 'like a mom, a second mom to me.'
protagonist.psychological_profile: Not applicable to a 12-year-old victim; for Hartman, no motive or psychology is documented in the sources and none is offered.
protagonist.mundane_humanizing_detail: She rode her bike home to pick up lunch, sandwiches, for her sisters, and her bike and the lunch were found at the park after she vanished.

individuals.name: Michella Evon Welch
individuals.specific_impact_suffered: Abducted from Puget Park on March 26, 1986 and killed; found the same night in the adjacent gulch. Officials said she had been sexually assaulted and died of blunt force trauma to the head.
individuals.humanizing_detail: Looking after her younger sisters; went home on her bike to fetch their lunch.

individuals.name: Barbara Leonard
individuals.specific_impact_suffered: Waited 32 years for an arrest and 36 for a conviction; attended the 2018 arraignment and the 2022 sentencing. (A KING 5 headline says a 'mother of murdered Tacoma girl' backed the 2019 DNA bill; it is not confirmed whether this was Barbara Leonard or Jennifer Bastian's mother, so the script does not claim it.)
individuals.humanizing_detail: Asked the judge for the maximum sentence while acknowledging it would not bring Michella back (paraphrase).
individuals.any_quotes_from_them: Paraphrase only (KING 5, 2022): he should be locked up and the key thrown away; it will not bring her back, but justice will have been served.

individuals.name: Nicole Eby
individuals.connection_to_protagonist: One of the two sisters at Puget Park that day
individuals.specific_impact_suffered: Lost her oldest sister as a child.
individuals.humanizing_detail: Said she forgives Hartman and wants to live her life fully because Michella never could.
individuals.any_quotes_from_them: 'like a mom, a second mom to me' (2022); 'He cut such a precious life short' (2018, wording varies by outlet)

individuals.name: Angela Velasquez
individuals.specific_impact_suffered: Lost her oldest sister as a child.
individuals.humanizing_detail: At sentencing she urged Hartman to rely on God (paraphrase).

individuals.name: Jennifer 'Jenni' Bastian
individuals.connection_to_protagonist: Separate 1986 case long assumed to be linked; NOT killed by Hartman
individuals.specific_impact_suffered: Disappeared while riding her bike in Point Defiance Park on August 4, 1986 and was found killed; Robert D. Washburn pleaded guilty in January 2019.
individuals.humanizing_detail: Her family and Tacoma detectives sponsored/pushed for 'Jennifer and Michella's Law' (2019).

collective_victims_if_applicable.group_description: Two Tacoma families (Welch and Bastian) whose cases were treated as one for decades
collective_victims_if_applicable.range_of_impacts: Decades without answers; the assumption of a single killer shaped both investigations until 2013.

characters.name: Detective Lindsey Wade (Tacoma Police Department)
characters.role_in_story: Cold case detective who reopened the case in 2009
characters.key_actions_they_took: Compiled a list of every man named in dozens of binders of reports, about 2,300 names; pushed re-testing; worked the genealogy lead.
characters.notable_quotes: 'That was a big turning point in the investigation.' (NBC News, 2019, about the DNA results)

characters.name: Detective Gene Miller (Tacoma Police Department)
characters.key_actions_they_took: Worked the Welch and Bastian cold cases with Wade (NBC News).

characters.name: Donald Ramsdell
characters.notable_quotes: Called the case a 'great example' of 'advancements in DNA identification and computer modeling combined with tried and true police techniques.'

characters.name: Parabon NanoLabs
characters.key_actions_they_took: 2016 Snapshot phenotyping reports on two separate male suspects; genealogists using GEDmatch data and public records built family trees (per the 2023 appellate opinion).

characters.name: Washington State Patrol Crime Laboratory
characters.key_actions_they_took: Developed the Bastian swimsuit profile in November 2013; on June 19, 2018 reported the napkin DNA matched the Welch crime-scene DNA.

characters.name: Judge Stanley Rumbaugh (Pierce County Superior Court)
characters.role_in_story: Presided over the March 22, 2022 stipulated-facts bench trial and sentencing
characters.key_actions_they_took: Found Hartman guilty of first-degree murder; sentenced him to 26 years and six months (some outlets: 320 months); said he would likely die in prison (paraphrase).

characters.name: Judge Elizabeth Martin (Pierce County Superior Court)
characters.role_in_story: Took Robert Washburn's guilty plea in the Bastian case
characters.key_actions_they_took: Read Washburn's written confession aloud in court.

characters.name: Robert Dwane Washburn
characters.role_in_story: Convicted killer of Jennifer Bastian (separate case)
characters.key_actions_they_took: Gave Tacoma police a DNA sample in May 2018 that matched the Bastian swimsuit; arrested in Eureka, Illinois; pleaded guilty in January 2019; sentenced to about 26.5-27 years.
characters.notable_quotes: Written statement (paraphrase): he wanted to spare the Bastian family a trial.

events.what_happened: Michella Evon Welch is born.
events.source: [34] Find a Grave memorial 20446637 (single source for middle name and birth year; age 12 confirmed by all outlets)

events.what_happened: Michella, a sixth grader, takes her two younger sisters to Puget Park; she rides her bike home to pick up lunch (sandwiches) and returns.
events.significance: Ordinary errand; her bike and the lunch later remain at the park.

events.what_happened: The younger sisters leave the park to use a restroom at a nearby business.
events.significance: The window in which Michella disappeared.
events.source: [6] ABC News 2018 (times differ slightly across accounts)

events.what_happened: The sisters return; Michella is gone; her bike and the lunch are at the park.
events.source: [6] ABC News; [36] Washington Post via Duluth News Tribune; [1] KING 5

events.what_happened: A search dog finds Michella's body in an isolated area of the gulch, more than a quarter mile from the play area, near a makeshift fire pit.
events.significance: Evidence collected, including DNA that would be preserved for decades.
events.source: [6] ABC News quoting police; [33] Oxygen (fire pit; some accounts say about 11:30 p.m.)

events.what_happened: Officials later said she had been sexually assaulted and died of blunt force trauma to the head.
Jennifer Bastian, 13, disappears while riding her bike; she is later found killed. Police long believe one man killed both girls.
events.significance: The single-killer assumption shapes both investigations.

events.what_happened: Detective Lindsey Wade reopens the cases and lists every man named in the files: about 2,300 names.
A male DNA profile is developed from Jennifer Bastian's swimsuit, untested for decades; it does not match the DNA from Michella's case.
Parabon releases Snapshot DNA phenotyping composites for two male suspects believed individually responsible for the two deaths.
events.source: [11] Parabon NanoLabs release; [12] Parabon case summary

events.what_happened: Police begin working with a genetic genealogist; a family tree built from public websites and run through a public database (GEDmatch) yields a 'significant match' to relatives.
events.source: [6] ABC News; [23] State v. Hartman (Wash. Ct. App. 2023)

events.what_happened: Arrest of Joseph James DeAngelo, the Golden State Killer suspect, publicly revealing genetic genealogy as a police tool.
events.significance: Context: Hartman's arrest came less than two months later.

events.what_happened: Tacoma police ask Robert Washburn for a DNA sample; it matches the Bastian swimsuit; he is arrested (May 10 or May 24 per different accounts) and extradited.
events.significance: Bastian case solved separately; no link to Michella.

events.what_happened: The genealogy points to Gary Hartman and his younger brother, who lived in Tacoma's North End in 1986; detectives begin surveillance.
A detective following Hartman collects a napkin he used and discarded at a restaurant.
events.significance: The discarded object that solved the case.
events.source: [5] KOMO court file; [3] Seattle Times; [6] ABC News

events.what_happened: The lab reports that DNA from the napkin matches the DNA from the Welch crime scene.
Hartman, 66, is arrested during a traffic stop and booked into the Pierce County Jail.
events.significance: 32 years and 86 days after Michella vanished.

events.what_happened: Hartman is charged with first-degree murder and first-degree rape; bail later set at $5 million.
Hartman pleads not guilty; Michella's mother Barbara Leonard and sisters attend.
Robert Washburn pleads guilty to first-degree murder of Jennifer Bastian before Judge Elizabeth Martin and is sentenced to about 26.5-27 years.
events.significance: Bastian case closed; reported date Jan. 25, 2019.

events.what_happened: 'Jennifer and Michella's Law' (HB 1326) is enacted, expanding DNA collection (including people convicted of felonies and indecent exposure, and samples from deceased offenders).

At a stipulated-facts bench trial lasting under two hours, Judge Stanley Rumbaugh finds Hartman, 70, guilty of first-degree (felony) murder, with rape as the underlying felony; Hartman says 'I'm so sorry'; he is sentenced to 26 years and six months.
events.significance: Conviction 36 years after the crime. NOTE: this was not a guilty plea and not in 2020.
events.source: [17] Seattle Times/AP; [18] KOMO; [19] KING 5; [20] Law&Crime (says 320 months); [23] State v. Hartman

events.location: Washington Court of Appeals, Division II
events.what_happened: In State v. Hartman, No. 56801-2-II, the court affirms the conviction, holding he had no privacy interest in DNA he abandoned or in his relatives' voluntarily uploaded DNA.
events.source: [23] FindLaw opinion; [24] State's answer to petition for review

events.what_happened: Hartman petitions for review (No. 102409-6); the State files an answer. Outcome not confirmed in this research.

the_moment.what_is_happening: Two little girls return from a restroom trip to find their big sister gone; her bike and their lunch are still at the park.
the_moment.what_makes_it_shocking: She was found that night in the wooded gulch next to the park.
the_moment.ironic_twist: The man convicted 36 years later was a nurse who, records show, lived less than two miles from the park in 1986; a used restaurant napkin finished the case.

cold_open_material.central_mystery_question: Who took a 12-year-old from a neighborhood park in broad daylight, and why did it take 32 years to find out?

the_method.technique_name: Investigative genetic genealogy plus discarded-DNA confirmation (STR comparison)
step_by_step_explanation: Crime-scene DNA preserved from 1986 produced a male profile that never matched anyone in the state or national offender databases (CODIS).
2013: separate testing of the Bastian swimsuit showed a different male DNA profile, proving two killers.
2016: Parabon phenotyping predicted traits of two different men; police began working with a genetic genealogist.
Genealogists compared the profile against a public database (GEDmatch), found several cousins of the killer, and built family trees with public records.
The trees converged on two brothers who lived in Tacoma's North End in 1986: Gary Hartman and his younger brother.
Surveillance in early June 2018; a detective collected a napkin Gary Hartman used at a restaurant.
Standard STR testing by the Washington State Patrol Crime Lab matched the napkin DNA to the crime-scene DNA on June 19, 2018.
the_method.why_it_worked: Relatives had voluntarily uploaded their DNA to GEDmatch; family trees narrowed the search to one household; a discarded napkin provided a legally collected confirmation sample.

technical_terms_to_explain.simple_explanation: The FBI-run DNA index of convicted offenders and crime scenes; it only finds people already in it.
The classic forensic DNA fingerprint: a short set of markers, good for a yes/no match, not for finding cousins.
Hundreds of thousands of markers, like the ones consumer DNA tests read, that can reveal distant relatives who then become clues on a family tree.
A free website (launched 2010) where people upload DNA results to find relatives.
A prediction of physical traits and ancestry from DNA; used here in 2016 to show two different men.
DNA left on an item someone throws away; courts in this case held he had no privacy interest in it.

the_method.scale_of_operation: About 2,300 names reviewed in the original files; decades of binders; a family tree built from several cousin matches.

systemic_failure.institution_that_failed: The early investigation and the forensic limits of the era (not a single institution).
systemic_failure.how_they_were_supposed_to_protect: Solve the case with the evidence collected in 1986.
systemic_failure.why_they_failed: In 1986 forensic DNA was in its infancy and the national DNA index did not exist until 1998; investigators assumed one killer for both Tacoma girls, and the Bastian swimsuit went untested until 2013.
specific_incompetence_examples: Two cases treated as one for about 27 years (1986-2013).
Bastian swimsuit evidence left untested for decades (NBC News).
Hartman's DNA was never in an offender database, so the profile never matched.
systemic_failure.ironic_details_about_the_failure: The man convicted lived less than two miles from the park in 1986 and worked for years as a nurse at a state hospital.

the_investigation.investigating_agency: Tacoma Police Department (cold case unit), Washington State Patrol Crime Lab, Parabon NanoLabs, Pierce County Prosecutor's Office
the_investigation.when_investigation_began: March 26, 1986; reopened by Detective Lindsey Wade in 2009
the_investigation.initial_wrong_assumptions: That one man killed both Michella Welch and Jennifer Bastian.
the_investigation.key_breakthrough: Genetic genealogy via GEDmatch cousins pointing to the Hartman brothers.
the_investigation.the_fatal_mistake: A napkin used and left at a restaurant during police surveillance.

the_confrontation.scene_description: Police stopped Hartman's vehicle and arrested him; he was booked into the Pierce County Jail. No further documented detail.
the_confrontation.protagonist_reaction: No documented statement at arrest in these sources.
the_confrontation.ironic_or_absurd_details: He was 66 and still working as a nurse at Western State Hospital.

charges_filed: First-degree murder (felony murder, rape as underlying felony)
First-degree rape (as filed in 2018; per the appellate opinion the murder charge used the rape as the predicate felony)
legal_resolution.trial_date_if_applicable: March 22, 2022: bench trial on stipulated facts, under two hours, Pierce County Superior Court
legal_resolution.notable_court_testimony: Hartman stipulated that the DNA from his used napkin matched DNA from Michella's body (per appellate opinion).

victim_impact_statements.key_quote: Paraphrase: lock him up and throw away the key; it won't bring her back, but justice will have been served.
'like a mom, a second mom to me'
Paraphrase: urged Hartman to rely on God.

legal_resolution.sentence_received: 26 years and six months in prison (most outlets); Law&Crime reports 320 months. The judge said he would likely die in prison.
legal_resolution.protagonist_statement_in_court: 'I'm so sorry.' He apologized to the family (KOMO).
legal_resolution.current_status: Convicted; serving his sentence in the Washington Department of Corrections (one secondary source names Airway Heights Corrections Center). Conviction affirmed by the Court of Appeals on August 22, 2023; outcome of the petition to the Washington Supreme Court (No. 102409-6) not confirmed.

details: The two 1986 Tacoma cases everyone believed were one were solved within weeks of each other in 2018 and turned out to involve two unrelated men.
The man convicted spent his career as a nurse, a caring profession.
A paper napkin at a restaurant did what 32 years of files could not.
The killer's own cousins, by uploading DNA to find family, led police to him.

universal_stakes.why_this_matters_to_viewer: A child was taken in daylight from a neighborhood park; the case shows how long unanswered questions last and how science and persistent detectives can still answer them.
universal_stakes.how_this_could_happen_to_them: Every parent who lets an older child watch younger siblings at a local park.
universal_stakes.lesson_or_warning: Evidence preserved properly and assumptions re-tested can solve cases decades later; a wrong assumption (one killer) can cost years.
universal_stakes.current_relevance: Genetic genealogy and its privacy limits; Washington's 2019 DNA law named after Jennifer and Michella.

unverified_claims: Exact sentence: 26 years 6 months (KING 5, KIRO, AP) vs 320 months (Law&Crime).
Exact time the body was found: 'just before 11 p.m.' (police via ABC) vs about 11:30 p.m. (other accounts).
Morning timeline: one account says she left the park around 10 a.m. to fetch lunch.
Witness under the Proctor bridge and suspect description: single secondary sources.
Airway Heights Corrections Center as current facility: single secondary source, possibly outdated.
Washburn arrest date (May 10 vs May 24, 2018) and exact sentence (26.5 vs 27 years).
Middle name 'Evon' and birth year 1973: Find a Grave only.
information_gaps: Outcome of Washington Supreme Court petition No. 102409-6.
Names and ages of the two younger sisters on the day (only adult names Nicole Eby and Angela Velasquez known).
Name of the restaurant and the genealogist.
Whether the rape count was dismissed as a separate count at the stipulated trial (one report says dropped).
questions_to_answer: Did the case brief premise ('pleaded guilty in 2020') come from confusion with Washburn's January 2019 plea? Verified: Hartman did NOT plead guilty; he was convicted at a stipulated-facts bench trial on March 22, 2022.
